text:
morgan: Quick sync — wanted to follow up on the canary/A-B fallback paths we prototyped. Found a few edge cases about split-state when route ownership changes mid-session.

sam: yeah saw that in perf tests. If a request gets mirrored then routed, backend state can diverge. We need a canonical decision point.

zane: proposal: attach a "switch_epoch" header to each request, set by the router at client-facing ingress. Router picks epoch once per session. If epoch mismatch, backend should invoke fallback logic instead of applying partial state.

ashley: can we avoid changing client SDKs? adding header seems invasive.

morgan: idea is router adds header automatically — user SDKs unchanged. SDKs only need to include session id for affinity. Router owns epoch.

leo: important: what about long-lived streaming sessions? If we switch mid-stream we must degrade gracefully, not drop.

sam: For streaming, fallback policy should allow a soft-continue: keep current stream for N tokens, open a parallel stream to fallback model and do a seamless mux once warm.

infra-bot: deploy:canary-v2 started on cluster-prod-3 — 4 pods

zane: rough policy yaml (thinking aloud):

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  mode: soft_mux
  grace_tokens: 32
  probe_timeout_ms: 200
  ownership_header: x-rw-epoch
  fallback_order: [compatible-quant, cheaper-variant, previous-production]
```

ashley: +1 to grace_tokens, but 32 might under-warm some large context models. Recommend making grace_tokens configurable per model profile.

morgan: agree. Also add telemetry hook: emit "epoch_switch" event with reason, from_router boolean, and current_latency_p50.

leo: how do we handle A/B experiments where we intentionally want divergence? We can't force fallback there.

sam: we add an opt-out flag in the route config: allow_divergence: true. Defaults to false for safety.

zane: race case: two routers with different epoch decisions because of slight clock skew — ensure epoch is monotonic token counter not wallclock.

morgan: good call. Use lease-based epoch tied to router leader election for a session. Router emits epoch=(leader_id:lease_counter).

ashley: ops question — how do oncall run a manual cutover rollback that respects this protocol?

morgan: runbook: 1) mark new leader as draining, 2) set route override to previous epoch, 3) trigger graceful-rolloff job which sets allow_divergence:true for 60s to flush experiments, 4) verify metrics. I'll draft.

leo: would like a small simulator to stress these transitions. I can hack one up to generate interleaved session traffic and epoch flips.

morgan: perfect. Action items: zane add epoch header to router proto, sam update policy schema to include per-model grace_tokens, ashley update runbook draft, leo build simulator. I'll open a follow-up RFC with these decisions.

sam: acked :thumbsup: 

infra-bot: deploy:canary-v2 pod-3 health=ok

morgan: thanks all. Leaving the thread open for any objections. If none by EOD I'll tag this to RFC queue.
